title: Predictive Value of the HALP Score for Post-Operative Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery.
summary: Post-operative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, occurring in 20% to 40% of patients and significantly increasing morbidity. The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score, a composite nutritional-inflammatory index, is a prognostic marker in cardiovascular disease. However, its predictive value for POAF remains unestablished. We aimed to evaluate the predictive performance of 5 nutritional-inflammatory indices (HALP, Naples score, Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index [SII], neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio [NPAR], and C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte [CALLY] index) for POAF and internally validate a novel prediction model incorporating HALP. Among 448 patients undergoing CABG, POAF occurred in 131 (29.2%). The HALP score demonstrated the highest discriminative ability (area under curve [AUC] 0.812), significantly (P < .001) outperforming Naples (AUC 0.676), NPAR (AUC 0.730), SII (AUC 0.726), and CALLY (AUC 0.684). Adding HALP to the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-derived base model significantly improved discriminative ability (AUC 0.813-0.897; P < .001) and net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities. The combined model achieved a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.885 with a calibration slope of 0.909, reflecting excellent internal validity. HALP was the strongest POAF predictor in the combined model. The HALP-integrated model showed excellent performance, offering a practical tool for preoperative POAF risk stratification.

title: Heart Failure Progression in the Setting of Persistent Atrial Fibrillation, Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes, and Malignancy-Related Limitations to Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy: A Case Report.
summary: Persistent atrial fibrillation and frequent premature ventricular complexes may contribute to worsening heart failure, particularly when malignancy limits guideline-directed medical therapy. In patients with progressive ventricular dysfunction and limited pharmacologic options, atrioventricular nodal ablation with cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation may provide durable rate control and support subsequent ventricular functional recovery.

title: Recurrence analysis of cardiac arrhythmias: A systematic review of methods, substrate characterisation and clinical translation.
summary: Cardiac arrhythmias are a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and catheter ablation depends on accurate identification of the underlying substrate. Cardiac signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, which limits Fourier-based analysis. Recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) and related recurrence methods make fewer assumptions, but their use in arrhythmia research has not been systematically synthesised. This review examines what recurrence analysis has demonstrated, how consistently its methods have been applied, and what remains before it can support clinical substrate characterisation. Of 309 records retrieved from four databases (207 after deduplication), 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and citation searching added one, giving 49. Each study was examined in full text for its signals, cohorts, embedding parameters, threshold selection, metrics and results, and assigned to one of six methodological categories. The three studies that tested recurrence against surrogate or shuffled data each found structure in fibrillatory signals that matched stochastic surrogates did not reproduce. Recurrence metrics and dominant frequency were weakly correlated and diverged in substrate characterisation, so they are not interchangeable. Threshold selection was the most consequential uncontrolled variable: five strategies were in use, ten of the 35 studies that apply a threshold reported no selection rule, and only three examined how their results depended on it. Determinism and laminarity, although the most frequently reported metrics, were not consistently the strongest discriminators. Clinical readiness is not established: only one study used recurrence mapping prospectively to guide ablation, in ten patients without randomisation. A shared threshold-selection standard and prospective multicentre validation are needed.

title: Clinician adherence to peri-procedural warfarin bridging guidelines for patients with atrial fibrillation enrolled in an anticoagulation management service.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 AHA/ACC/HRS guidelines recommend against peri-procedural bridging of warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based solely on CHA₂DS₂-VASc score without additional thromboembolic (TE) risk factors. At our institution, decisions regarding bridging in moderate-to-high TE risk AF patients who require anticoagulation interruption incorporate patient-specific factors.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate adherence to institutional peri-procedural guidelines and associated TE and bleeding events.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study included AF patients receiving warfarin for stroke prevention enrolled in the anticoagulation management service. Patients had moderate-to-high TE risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5 or other TE risk factors) and underwent moderate-to-high bleeding risk procedures between August 2023 and August 2024. Major outcomes included a composite of TE events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accidents, or transient ischemic attack) and a composite of International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) major and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB) events within 30 days post-procedure. Minor outcomes included individual components of the composite outcomes and adherence to the institutional guideline.

RESULTS: Of the 145 procedures, bridging therapy was used in 87 (60%) and omitted in 58 (40%), with 92.4% compliance to institutional guidance. No TE events were observed. Of 21 bleeding events, one ISTH major bleed occurred in the bridging group and was attributed to the procedure, while 20 were CRNMB events. There were 15 (17.4%) CRNMB events in the bridging group and 5 (8.6%) in the non-bridging group.

CONCLUSION: High adherence to institutional bridging guidelines was observed. A trend towards fewer bleeding events with no increased TE events was found in the non-bridging group in patients with moderate-to-high TE risk.

title: Concomitant Balloon-in-Basket Pulsed Field Ablation and Next-Generation Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Acute Procedural Success and Early Safety and Effectiveness results from the Prospective Multicenter CLEAR Study
Safety, Efficacy and Cost of Same-Day Discharge after Pulsed Field Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Sub-study of the Multicentre SENTINEL Registry
Transitioning towards life-cycle management and burden monitoring of atrial fibrillation.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses a significant burden on public health, being associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. In most cases, disease progression follows a continuum, ranging from a predominantly electrical disorder to late stages characterized by profound disruption of atrial architecture and advanced atrial cardiomyopathy.

AREAS COVERED: Common cardiovascular risk factors play a pivotal role in the progression and self-perpetuation of AF by promoting left atrial remodeling, creating the substrate necessary for the maintenance of the arrhythmia. Correction of these risk factors, together with rhythm-control strategies, can delay and, in some cases, interrupt disease progression while improving patients' quality of life. Catheter ablation, when combined with life-style modifications and risk factors management, has the potential to positively modify the arrhythmogenic substrate that favors AF and could promote reverse atrial remodeling.

EXPERT OPINION: Comprehensive management of risk factors and comorbidities, together with novel ablation techniques (e.g. pulsed field ablation) and the development of atrial-selective antiarrhythmic drugs, may further improve AF care. In addition, redefining long-term rhythm control success from freedom from AF recurrence to AF burden may allow better patient stratification, inform therapeutic decisions, and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

title: Extent of posterior wall lesion following pulmonary vein isolation with pentaspline pulsed field and cryoballoon ablation: the potential role of deployment technique.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using cryoballoon (CB) or pulsed field ablation (PFA) with a pentaspline catheter achieves similar efficacy in atrial fibrillation (AF), but lesion extension on the left atrial posterior wall (LAPW) may differ. Pentaspline-PFA (P-PFA) has been reported to create broader LAPW lesions, potentially leaving narrow viable corridors that have been hypothesized to be proarrhythmic.

OBJECTIVE: To descriptively compare the extent of chronic unintended left atrial posterior wall isolation after PVI with P-PFA and CB ablation.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center ambispective study including consecutive patients undergoing repeat left atrial mapping after index PVI with either P-PFA, using a protocol designed to ensure catheter alignment with the pulmonary veins, or CB. Patients with additional LA ablation between index procedure and remapping, unrelated LAPW scarring, or posterior pulmonary vein gaps were excluded. The primary endpoint was isolated LAPW area. Secondary endpoints included percentage of isolated LAPW and minimum residual corridor width.

RESULTS: Seventy-four patients were included in the analysis: 49 P-PFA and 25 CB. Mean age was 64.2 ± 10.0 years, 64.9% were male, and 55.4% had persistent AF. Isolated LAPW area was 8.3 ± 4.0 cm2 in the P-PFA group and 9.5 ± 3.9 cm2 in the CB group, with no statistically significant difference detected between groups (mean difference -1.26 cm2, 95% CI: -3.22 to 0.70; p = 0.203). The percentage of isolated LAPW area was 39.9 ± 17.6% vs. 38.9 ± 14.9% (p = 0.805), and minimum residual corridor width was 19.7 ± 9.9 vs. 18.6 ± 11.0 mm (p = 0.671), respectively. P-PFA was associated with shorter procedure time (44.2 ± 10.2 vs. 65.8 ± 24.6 min; p < 0.001), shorter LA dwell time (38.1 ± 9.6 vs. 60.6 ± 20.5 min; p < 0.001), lower fluoroscopy time (5.3 ± 3.9 vs. 13.0 ± 9.7 min; p < 0.001), and lower dose-area product [5.3 (2.8-9.7) vs. 19.3 (6.5-31.0) Gy·cm2; p < 0.001].

CONCLUSION: In this descriptive, hypothesis-generating study, no statistically significant difference in chronic LAPW isolation extent was detected between P-PFA and CB ablation. These findings support the hypothesis that catheter deployment technique may influence posterior wall lesion geometry, warranting confirmation in adequately powered prospective studies.

title: Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium.

OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia.

RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35).

CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

title: Sequential multimodality imaging-guided transseptal strategy for cryoballoon ablation in cor triatriatum sinister.
summary:
To describe a sequential multimodality imaging strategy for transseptal access during cryoballoon ablation in a patient with cor triatriatum sinister (CTS).

METHODS: A 55-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and CTS underwent preprocedural cardiac computed tomography (CCT), followed by real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), contrast confirmation, and fluoroscopic guidance during the procedure.

RESULTS: CCT demonstrated pulmonary vein drainage into a Proximal Chamber (Posterior-Superior), separated from the Distal Chamber (Anterior-Inferior) by a membrane. Real-time TEE identified and confirmed an anterosuperior transseptal site, with septal tenting before needle passage. After a single BRK needle puncture, contrast confirmed access to the pulmonary-vein-containing chamber, allowing advancement of the FlexCath Advance catheter (Medtronic) and cryoballoon isolation of all 4 pulmonary veins without procedural complications.

CONCLUSION: In CTS, transseptal access should be tailored to the individual atrial anatomy. Sequential use of CCT, real-time TEE, contrast, and fluoroscopy can provide complementary information at the successive stages of the procedure.

title: Inferolateral ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Secondary to Suspected Coronary Embolism in a Patient with Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: A Case Report.
summary: Coronary embolism is an underrecognized nonatherosclerotic cause of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), most commonly associated with atrial fibrillation. We report a 76-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation who presented with acute substernal chest pain and inferolateral STEMI. Coronary angiography demonstrated a 100% thrombotic occlusion of the distal right posterolateral ventricular branch with otherwise nonobstructive coronary artery disease. In the setting of an abrupt distal coronary occlusion, minimal underlying atherosclerotic disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and fulfillment of the Shibata diagnostic criteria, coronary embolism was considered the most likely mechanism. Long-term anticoagulation was continued, and the patient remained asymptomatic at 1-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of suspected coronary embolism in patients presenting with STEMI, atrial fibrillation, and minimal underlying coronary artery disease.

title: Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes and Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) are often observed in patients undergoing ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the relationship between AF ablation and PVCs is uncertain. The purpose of this study was to examine the prevalence of frequent PVCs before and after catheter ablation of AF.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing ablation of AF at two tertiary centers. All patients undergoing initial or repeat ablation of AF were eligible. Patients were followed in AF clinics before and after ablation with routine ambulatory ECG monitoring.

RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 421 patients (mean 63 years, 33% female, 57% paroxysmal). At baseline, 18.4% and 4.7% had ≥ 1% and ≥ 5% PVCs respectively. In the 179 days post-ablation, 9.0% developed new onset ≥ 1% PVCs, whereas 10.9% of patients had regression from ≥ 1% to < 1% PVCs. In the total follow up period of 2 years, there was a significant increase in the proportion of patients with ≥ 1% PVCs. Multivariable modeling revealed baseline PVC burden and hypertension as the only predictors of an increasing PVC burden in the post-ablation period.

CONCLUSION: Frequent PVCs are highly prevalent among patients undergoing AF ablation. However, there was no signal of an increase in frequent PVCs in the immediate post-ablation period.

title: Decoding Atrial Fibrillation Heterogeneity: A Nationwide Phenome-Wide Association Study in England.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Age and sex influence atrial fibrillation (AF) prevalence and outcomes, yet comprehensive data on sex- and age-specific health care utilization in patients newly diagnosed with AF remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to address this gap using a phenome-wide association study (Phe-WAS) approach.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using nationwide Clinical Practice Research Datalink data linked to Hospital Episodes Statistics. Adults diagnosed with AF between 1998 and 2016 (n = 199,433) were matched 1:1 by age and sex to non-AF control subjects. Primary and secondary care interactions 5 years post diagnosis were analyzed using Phe-WAS with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios for conditions in AF vs control groups, stratified by sex and age. Associations were assessed for novelty through literature review and causality using published Mendelian randomization studies.

RESULTS: Patients with AF had higher rates of cardiovascular and noncardiovascular conditions than control subjects, with marked sex- and age-specific patterns. Women had more bleeding complications, pneumonia, Clostridium difficile enterocolitis, cholangitis, and electrolyte disturbances, whereas men had higher rates of alcohol-related disorders, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, and cardiomyopathy. Younger patients with AF (<50 years) more often had alcohol-related mental and behavioral disorders, gout, and dilated cardiomyopathy, while older patients (>60 years) more often had heart failure, ischemic stroke, renal failure, and respiratory infections. Of 51 phenotypes more common in AF, 28 were previously reported, and 23 were potentially novel. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested AF was causal for 19 associations.

CONCLUSIONS: This Phe-WAS demonstrates the broad spectrum of health care interactions in AF beyond traditional cardiovascular complications.

title: The Vein of Marshall Promotes Re-Entry After Pulmonary Vein Reconnection.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia recurrence remains a major limitation of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Pulmonary vein (PV) reconnection and epicardial connections from the left atrium (LA) to the vein of Marshall (VoM) and coronary sinus (CS) in proximity to mitral valve are important contributors. We hypothesized that VoM facilitates arrhythmia induction through interaction with the epicardial region encircled by wide antral circumferential ablation (WACA).

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to systematically evaluate the combined effect of PV reconnection and epicardial VoM connectivity on the occurrence of sustained postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia using in silico models.

METHODS: Bilayer biatrial models were constructed from electroanatomical and computed tomographic data of 10 patients with AF. Post-AF electrical remodeling and substrate remodeling following the low voltage area distribution, and left-sided WACA were incorporated. Segments of WACA lesions were sequentially restored to simulate PV reconnection. Three connectivity scenarios were evaluated: intact CS-VoM-LA epicardial connection, CS-LA connection only, and no epicardial connections. Sustained re-entry (>10 seconds) was the primary endpoint, and connectivity conditions were compared using patient-level paired vulnerability. Induction of any arrhythmia, tachycardia cycle length, and stable rotor number were secondary outcomes.

RESULTS: Sustained re-entry occurred at 92 of 294 (31.3%) reconnection sites with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity, 37 of 294 (12.6%) with CS-LA connectivity only, and 29 of 294 (9.9%) without epicardial connectivity. Patient-level paired analysis showed 19.9-percentage-point and 22.7-percentage-point higher vulnerability with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity compared with CS-LA connectivity alone (95% CI: 7.1-37.3 percentage points) and no epicardial connectivity (95% CI: 7.4-41.3 percentage points), respectively. Mean tachycardia cycle length in the LA was 258.0 ± 25.7 milliseconds, 255.0 ± 31.4 milliseconds, and 251.0 ± 33.9 milliseconds across the 3 scenarios; the average number of stable rotors was 0.6 ± 0.3, 0.7 ± 0.2, and 0.4 ± 0.2, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The VoM is a critical epicardial driver of arrhythmia after incomplete WACA, underscoring the importance of its targeted ablation.

title: Pulsed Field Ablation of the Left Atrial Appendage Before Mechanical Closure to Reduce Peri-Device Leak (STUN-AF).
summary:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (LAAC) is plagued by late peri-device leak. We posited that appendage contraction prevents full LAA seal, so conversely, LAA stunning with pulsed field ablation (PFA) of the LAA (left atrial appendage ablation [LAAA]) might promote rapid appendage thrombosis/obliteration.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to assess the impact of LAAA during concomitant procedures on eliminating leaks.

METHODS: At 3 centers, consecutive patients undergoing concomitant PFA and LAAC also underwent LAAA or did not undergo LAAA, at operator discretion. Initial (∼3-4 months) (29% transesophageal echocardiography/71% computed tomography) and 12-month imaging were compared with a primary composite outcome of LAA patency, defined as either detectable flow into the LAA or evidence of echo-free space/contrast medium behind the device.

RESULTS: Among 317 total patients undergoing PFA and LAAC, including 222 patients who underwent LAAA and 95 who did not (control patients), all underwent initial imaging and 126 reached 12-month imaging follow-up. Device compression was 28% with LAAA vs 25% without LAAA (P < 0.001). Implantation success was 100%. The periprocedural adverse event rate was 2% in both groups. The primary composite outcome of LAA patency was significantly reduced with LAAA vs no-LAAA, both at 3-4 months (29% vs 64%; P < 0.001) and at 12 months (4% vs 42%; P < 0.001). Device-related thrombus rates were low and similar (2.3% vs 3.2%; P = 0.7). A validation subset including only patients with alternating LAAA assignment (LAAA: n = 59; no-LAAA: n = 63) again revealed that LAAA was associated with reduced LAA patency (3-4 months: 34% vs 51%; P = 0.06; 12 months: 8% vs 36%; P = 0.2). Final LAA e' velocity was significantly different between groups (17 ± 7 vs 34 ± 16 cm/s; P < 0.001), with higher velocity associated with LAA patency (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: PFA of the LAA has potential to reduce LAA patency during device-based LAAC.

title: Neighborhood Disadvantage and Unequal Detection of Atrial Fibrillation.
Race- and Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants of Health in Diagnosis and Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
IMPORTANCE: Early diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF) is critical for preventing stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Understanding patterns in diagnosis and treatment of AF may improve detection and reduce disparities.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interactions between race and ethnicity and neighborhood social determinants of health on AF diagnosis and treatment.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Retrospective cohort study using administrative claims for greater Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, area residents aged 18 years or older from Independence Blue Cross from 2017 to 2021. Baseline characteristics were assessed in 2017, and participants were followed up from 2018 through 2021. Data were analyzed from October 2023 to July 2026.

EXPOSURES: Exposures included Non-Hispanic Black race and ethnicity, neighborhood-level social determinants of health as measured by the social barrier index (SBI), and the interaction between the two.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was AF diagnosis ascertained from International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision diagnosis codes. The secondary outcome was anticoagulant prescription among individuals with AF diagnoses as ascertained from pharmacy claims.

RESULTS: Of the 504 876 patients included, the mean (SD) age was 48 (18) years; 267 596 (53.0%) were female; 67 362 (13.3%) non-Hispanic Black, and 437 514 (86.7%) were non-Hispanic White. A total of 27 249 patients (5.1%) were diagnosed with AF during the study period. Non-Hispanic Black patients were less likely to be diagnosed with AF compared with non-Hispanic White patients (odds ratio [OR], 0.91; 95% CI, 0.82-1.00). The relative difference increased with increased SBI (which denotes more vulnerable neighborhoods) as shown by a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95). Among those diagnosed with AF, 15 722 (58%) had an anticoagulant prescription. There was a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.00-1.20), suggesting that filled prescription patterns differed by race and ethnicity with SBI. For Black individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with decreased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.90-0.99). For White individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with increased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03-1.07).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cohort study of Medicare Advantage and commercially insured individuals found that AF diagnosis rates declined with worsening neighborhood-level disadvantage among non-Hispanic Black individuals but increased among non-Hispanic White individuals. Conditional on diagnoses, rates of prescription of anticoagulants were similar across race and ethnicity groups. Targeted interventions, especially in more marginalized neighborhoods, are needed to increase detection of AF.

title: Aveir VR for Atrial Leadless Pacing in Young Patients.
summary: Atrial Leadless pacemaker implantspresent a new treatment for sinus node dysfunction in complex cardiac anatomies. The Aveir-VR single chamber pacemaker can be placed in the atrium to control atrial flutter, or in the ventricle to control bradycardia. In this case report, we present four cases of the implantation of the Aveir VR in the atrium of male pediatric patients to treat sinus node dysfunction. Retrospective review of patients with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and atrially placed Aveir-VRs was performed at UC Davis between April 2024 and April 2026. Femoral access was the route of implantation for all 5 patients. Trans-esophageal echocardiography was used in all cases. The patients' ages ranged between 14-17-years and follow-up appointments were held between 1-23-months. Immediately post-procedure, impedances were 380-1460 Ohms, thresholds at 0.4 ms were 2.25-3.5 V, and P-waves were between 1.7-3 mV. Follow-up impedance was between 390-720 Ohms for the patients, thresholds were 0.5-1.25 V at 0.2-0.4 ms, P-waves were between 4.5-9.1 mV, and pacing percentages were between 12-69%. This case series demonstrates the successful implant of Aveir VR leadless pacemaker in five young patients for sinus node dysfunction.

title: Acute Changes in Left Atrial Appendage Flow Velocity During Pulsed Field Ablation: An Intraprocedural Intracardiac Echocardiography Study
summary: **Background:** Despite the close anatomical relationship between the left pulmonary veins (PVs) and the left atrial appendage (LAA), acute changes in LAA flow during pulsed field ablation (PFA) remain poorly characterized. **Objectives:** To characterize acute intraprocedural changes in LAA flow and transmitral filling during PFA for atrial fibrillation (AF) using paired intracardiac echocardiography (ICE). **Methods:** Patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing PFA were prospectively enrolled if they were in sinus rhythm at the beginning of the procedure. ICE was performed immediately before and after PFA to assess LAA emptying velocity (LAAEv), LAA filling velocity (LAAFv), transmitral E- and A-wave velocities, and E-wave deceleration time (EDT). Paired pre-to-post PFA changes were assessed, followed by a sensitivity analysis using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and exploratory subgroup analyses. **Results:** Among 98 patients, LAAEv increased from 35.45 to 40.00 cm/s immediately after PFA (estimated paired increase, 4.95 cm/s; 95% CI, 2.35-7.80; P less than 0.001), while LAAFv increased by 4.36 cm/s (95% CI, 1.81-6.91; P=0.001). E-wave velocity increased by 8.69 cm/s and EDT decreased by 31.73 ms (both P less than 0.001), whereas A-wave velocity did not change significantly (P=0.08). In the ANCOVA model, changes in heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and vasopressor use were not significantly associated with changes in LAAEv. A marked acute reduction in LAAEv (20% or greater) occurred in 12 patients (12.2%). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. **Conclusions:** LAA flow velocities increased acutely after PFA, accompanied by changes in transmitral filling, although a minority of patients showed a marked acute reduction in LAA emptying.

title: Evaluation and management of clinically significant arrhythmias in the early neonatal period: a single-center retrospective study of NICU-admitted neonates
summary: Abstract Introduction Arrhythmias in the neonatal period are abnormalities of heart rate that carry a significant risk of mortality and morbidity if not diagnosed early. There is limited evidence on the characteristics, frequency and treatment approaches of arrhythmias in the early neonatal period (0–7 days). Materials and methods In this retrospective study, we analyzed the data of 40 neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)-admitted neonates diagnosed with clinically significant arrhythmias in the early neonatal period between December 2017 and November 2024. Sex, birth weight, clinical signs and symptoms, electrocardiography (ECG), Holter ECG, echocardiography (ECHO) findings, treatment and follow-up outcomes were evaluated. Results Non-benign arrhythmia was detected in 40 (0.97%) of 4126 neonates admitted to the NICU in the early neonatal period. The median follow-up period was 30.5 months (range, 0.25-67 months). The most common arrhythmia type was supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and the most common subtype was atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT). In the bradyarrhythmia group, non-conducted premature atrial contractions (non-conducted PACs) and complete atrioventricular (AV) block were detected. Arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy (AIC) was present in eight patients (20%), and congenital heart disease (CHD) was found in five patients (12.5%). Initial treatments included vagal maneuvers, adenosine, amiodarone, and flecainide. One patient died due to heart failure. During the follow-up period, SVT recurrence was observed in four cases, all of whom achieved rhythm control with antiarrhythmic therapy. Conclusions Our study emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in improving the prognosis of clinically significant arrhythmias in the early neonatal period. Non-conducted PACs can be successfully managed with medical treatment when they cause hemodynamic disturbances. These contractions may lead to clinical conditions requiring early intervention, and appropriate treatment can improve cardiac function. The low recurrence and mortality rates in patients without complex congenital heart disease in our study group suggest that arrhythmias in the early neonatal period may have a favorable prognosis with correct diagnosis and treatment. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Mitral Annular Disjunction: Regional Strain Abnormalities Associated With Life-Threatening Ventricular Arrhythmias.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been linked to malignant ventricular arrhythmias in mitral valve prolapse, but the mechanisms and risk predictors are not well established. We aimed to identify clinical and echocardiographic factors with a focus on left ventricular (LV) strain.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 69 patients with MAD confirmed on echocardiogram. Clinical data and echocardiographic measurements were collected, including chamber dimensions, MAD distance, mitral regurgitation grade, and 2D global and segmental longitudinal strain by speckle-tracking. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to determine independent predictors of arrhythmia.

RESULTS: All patients had preserved LV ejection fraction. Patients with arrhythmias demonstrated trends toward larger chamber dimensions and a larger MAD distance. Global longitudinal strain did not significantly differ between groups. Differences between patients with and without life-threatening arrhythmias localized specifically to the inferolateral region at the mid-ventricular level, where mid-inferolateral strain was significantly worse in arrhythmic patients (median -12.6% [IQR 13.5] vs. -18.9% [IQR 6.0], p = 0.0069). In univariate models, factors associated with arrhythmias included larger LV chamber diameters, greater MAD distance, a history of syncope, and worse strain in the mid-inferior and mid-inferolateral segments. On exploratory multivariate analysis, mid-inferolateral strain impairment appears to be independently associated with LTA (OR 1.11 per 1% strain increase, p = 0.012).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with MAD, impaired mid-inferolateral segment strain was associated with LTA, suggesting that regional myocardial deformation may provide incremental arrhythmic risk stratification beyond global measures. These findings are, however, exploratory, hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts with independent validation to ascertain clinical utility.

title: Ventricular arrhythmic burden before and after mitral valve repair in mitral valve prolapse: the role of mitral annular disjunction.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is increasingly recognized as an arrhythmogenic condition, with a subset of patients exhibiting ventricular arrhythmias beyond the hemodynamic effects of mitral regurgitation (MR). Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been proposed as a structural marker associated with arrhythmic risk, but its relationship with postoperative ventricular arrhythmias after mitral valve repair remains incompletely understood. We aimed to evaluate changes in ventricular arrhythmic burden following mitral valve repair and to investigate the association between preoperative MAD and postoperative ventricular ectopy.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 77 patients with MVP who underwent surgical mitral valve repair for severe MR and had both preoperative and postoperative 24-h Holter recordings. Premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden and ventricular arrhythmias were assessed before and after surgery. MAD was evaluated retrospectively using transthoracic echocardiography. Multivariable linear regression, sensitivity analyses, and sequential model comparison were performed to evaluate the independent and incremental association of MAD with postoperative PVC burden.

RESULTS: Overall PVC burden decreased significantly after mitral valve repair. Patients with preoperative MAD had a substantially higher PVC burden both before surgery [7,800 (7,000-9,575) vs. 4,200 (3,200-6,200) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] and after surgery [5,700 (5,175-6,425) vs. 2,200 (1,800-3,500) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] than those without MAD. The relative reduction in PVC burden was comparable between groups (-35.4 ± 20.6% vs. -39.5 ± 29.5%, p = 0.113). In multivariable analysis, preoperative MAD remained independently associated with higher postoperative PVC burden after adjustment for clinical covariates, prolapse phenotype, residual mitral regurgitation, and baseline PVC burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Mitral valve repair was associated with a significant reduction in ventricular ectopic burden in patients with MVP. However, preoperative MAD identified patients with a higher postoperative ventricular ectopic burden despite a similar proportional reduction in PVCs. These findings support the potential value of postoperative rhythm surveillance in patients with preoperative MAD.

title: Left bundle branch area pacing induced dual bundle branches non-reentrant bigeminy and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy: a case report.
summary: A 76-year-old woman with intermittent advanced atrioventricular block from a previous left septal accessory pathway and atrioventricular (AV) nodal slow pathway ablation for supraventricular tachycardia was referred for pacing. Her echocardiogram showed no structural abnormality and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBaP) was achieved successfully, although frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) were observed during the procedure. In the interrogation before discharge, asymptomatic ST-segment elevation on the precordial electrocardiogram (ECG) necessitated an emergent coronary angiography. No significant stenosis or spasm of coronary arteries was found, while left ventriculography revealed apical dyskinesis suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. On closer inspection, frequent monomorphic PVCs developed after each pacing beat and formed a regular bigeminy pattern, indicating rapid LBB stimulation, and the facilitated slow conduction along the adjacent bundle branches induced the dual ventricular response. The resultant frequent desynchronized ventricular activation may have contributed to the stress for cardiac decompensation. Beta blocker was titrated to alter the critical time period matched for the repetitive activation pattern and to suppress sympathetic tension. The bigeminy was eliminated ultimately, and repositioning of the lead was avoided. The ventricular wall motion and LVEF recovered within months. This case highlights the importance of close observation of electrocardiographic monitoring after pacing. Despite the potential benefits for future cardiac function and lower pro-arrhythmic effect than routine pacing modalities, LBBaP may still be associated with new-onset arrhythmia and myocardial injury considering the baseline impairment of the electrical or anatomical substrate. Individualized management should be tailored according to specific scenarios.

title: High-Grade Atrioventricular Block and Recurrent Cardiac Arrest in Suspected Isolated Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac sarcoidosis may cause advanced atrioventricular block, ventricular dysfunction, and sudden cardiac death. Isolated cardiac presentations are diagnostically challenging when histologic confirmation and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography are unavailable.

CASE SUMMARY: An 18-year-old woman with recurrent syncope developed high-grade atrioventricular block and recurrent brady-asystolic cardiac arrest requiring temporary transvenous pacing. Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated regional septal thickening, basal to midseptal midmyocardial late gadolinium enhancement and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 38.9%. No extracardiac sarcoid pattern or biopsy target was identified. Giant cell myocarditis and inherited cardiomyopathy remained important alternative diagnoses. She received corticosteroid therapy and subsequently underwent cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac sarcoidosis should remain a diagnostic consideration in young patients with malignant conduction disease and inflammatory cardiomyopathy, while important mimics must be actively considered.

title: Pacing Related Conduction Delay as an Indicator of Intramural Site of Origin of Focal Ventricular Arrhythmias.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The diagnosis of intramural focal ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be challenging and is often made in retrospect after a long ineffective procedure.

OBJECTIVES: In this cohort of patients, we aim to assess the value of pace-mapping (PM), stimulus-QRS interval (S-QRS interval), and electrogram (EGM)-QRS intervals to identify the site of origin (SOO) of focal VAs.

METHODS: In a consecutive series of 46 patients with frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), activation mapping and PM were performed to identify VA target sites. VA target sites were defined as sites with matching PM (≥10/12 leads) and/or sites with the earliest activation time. S-QRS interval and bipolar activation time at target sites were assessed and correlated with acute outcomes. If ablation at a target site failed, alternative sites were sought in adjacent anatomical structures. An intramural origin was defined as a VA with early activation time without a matching PM.

RESULTS: Matching PMs were identified for 32 VAs in 30 of the 46 patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed at the target site/PVC level and demonstrated that a mismatch between S-QRS and EGM-QRS of >26 milliseconds distinguished effective from ineffective ablation sites with a matching PM (area under the curve: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.94-1; sensitivity: 100%; specificity: 88.9%). A mismatch was present in 9 patients, and radiofrequency ablation failed in 8/9 of them. Alternate sites with early activation times (-48.4 ± 37.39 milliseconds) without matching PM, where radiofrequency eliminated the PVCs, were identified in 5/8 patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Conduction delay with matching PMs but late activation indicates a deeper SOO. A cutoff value of >26 milliseconds between S-QRS and EGM-QRS intervals identified deeper-seated VA target sites. This required further mapping to identify alternative ablation sites. A matching PM may not always be indicative of the SOO in patients with PVCs.

title: Cardiac screening in the young for the detection of cardiovascular disease and prevention of sudden cardiac death.
summary: Sudden cardiac death in the young is often due to silent inherited cardiac conditions. Although evidence increasingly supports cardiac screening as a preventative strategy, policies and frameworks differ globally. Structured screening frameworks that utilise AI-enabled technologies show great potential for enhancing disease detection and risk prediction.

title: Prolonged QT Interval in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Determinants and Reversibility.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: QT interval prolongation is a common electrocardiographic abnormality in hospitalized patients, associated with malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Its determinants in internal medicine, and the reliability of correction formulas used to identify it, remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 277 patients hospitalized with QTc prolongation - defined by Bazett correction (QTcB >450 ms in men; ≥460 ms in women) - between January 2016 and December 2023. QTc was independently calculated using Bazett (QTcB) and Framingham (QTcF) formulas, and agreement between the two was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression (complete-case analysis) explored predictors of QTcF-confirmed prolongation, and reversibility was assessed by repeat ECG performed after correction of the underlying reversible cause, or within 72 hours when no such cause was identified.

RESULTS: Mean age was 59.2 ±17.2 years, with a slight female predominance (54.2%). Only 78 patients (28.1%) had QTcF-confirmed prolongation despite all meeting QTcB inclusion criteria. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +31.7 ms between QTcB and QTcF (SD 18.9; 95% limits of agreement: -5.3 to +68.7 ms), strongly correlated with heart rate (r=0.92, p<0.001): the overcorrection increased from +3.6 ms at heart rate <70 bpm to +64.4 ms at >110 bpm. QTcB normalized on the follow-up ECG in 68.2% of patients. In a complete-case multivariable model (n=96 with available serum bicarbonate), no variable reached conventional statistical significance; serum bicarbonate (OR=1.121 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 0.991-1.268; p=0.069) and hypertension (OR=2.522; 95% CI: 0.875-7.275; p=0.087) showed borderline associations with QTcF-confirmed prolongation. In an exploratory analysis of the diabetic subgroup (n=148), peripheral neuropathy (DN4 ≥4) was associated with a 15.8 ms higher mean QTcB (age-adjusted 95% CI: 4.7-27.0 ms; p=0.006).

CONCLUSION: Bazett's formula substantially and heart-rate-dependently overestimates QT prolongation compared with the Framingham formula, a discrepancy now precisely quantified. QT prolongation in hospitalized internal medicine patients is predominantly acquired and reversible. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was associated with higher QTcB values in an exploratory analysis. Serum bicarbonate showed only a non-significant trend toward association with QTcF-confirmed prolongation after complete-case multivariable adjustment; this hypothesis warrants confirmation in prospective studies with complete acid-base characterization before any clinical application.

title: Trajectories of kinesiophobia over the first six months after cardiac pacemaker or defibrillator implantation: clinical, psychological, and rehabilitation predictors and their relation to functional capacity.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Kinesiophobia, an excessive fear of physical movement, is common after implantation of a cardiac pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator and may limit rehabilitation and recovery. Because fear of movement changes over time, a single measurement cannot capture how it evolves. We aimed to identify distinct trajectories of kinesiophobia during the first six months after implantation, to relate them to functional capacity, and to identify baseline factors that predict an unfavourable course.

METHODS: In a single centre retrospective cohort based on routinely collected structured follow-up data, 160 consecutive patients undergoing first implantation of a pacemaker or defibrillator were assessed 24 to 48 h after the procedure and again at 1, 3, and 6 months. Kinesiophobia was measured with the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia Heart and functional capacity with the six-minute walk distance. Group-based trajectory modelling identified latent trajectories. Baseline characteristics were compared across classes, and multinomial logistic regression identified independent predictors of class membership.

RESULTS: Mean kinesiophobia fell from 42.9 to 35.2 over six months, and the proportion above the high-fear threshold fell from 76.2% to 37.5%. Three trajectories emerged: low and declining (28.8%), moderate and declining (45.0%), and high and persistent (26.2%). The persistent group stayed above the clinical threshold throughout and walked the shortest distance at every visit. Compared with the low group, independent predictors of a persistent course were higher depression (odds ratio 2.26), higher anxiety (1.68), lower exercise self-efficacy (0.89), shorter baseline walk distance (0.55 per 10 m), and absence of exercise guidance (0.04 for having received guidance).

CONCLUSION: Kinesiophobia after device implantation follows three trajectories, separated mainly by the overall level of fear. About one quarter of patients remain persistently fearful and physically limited; they can be identified early by distress, low self-efficacy, poor functional capacity, and lack of exercise guidance. Early screening and targeted exercise-based rehabilitation are warranted.

title: [Psychotherapeutic interventions for reducing stress in patients with cardiac arrhythmias].
summary: Cardiac arrhythmias may remain asymptomatic, but they can also be experienced as palpitations or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) shocks that feel existentially threatening. Even harmless arrhythmias can trigger intense anxiety reactions, including traumatic processing. Therefore, in addition to cardiological diagnostics and treatment, an integrative psychocardiological perspective is needed. From a cardiological point of view, the symptom burden should be reduced, for example, by avoiding substances that promote arrhythmias, treating underlying diseases, and-particularly in ICD patients-optimizing potassium levels. Psychoeducation is central: patients should understand why extrasystoles may be experienced as missed beats, strong palpitations, or a sensation of the "heart beating up into the throat." Equally important is discussing the vicious circle of anxiety: tension, worry, and self-monitoring lower the threshold for perception; perceived cardiac symptoms then intensify anxiety and autonomic arousal. Since these signals are interoceptive, avoidance is not possible, and patients should be taught routines that help them break out of the anxiety cycle. Special attention should be given to patients after an ICD shock or cardiac arrest. They may develop posttraumatic stress disorder induced by the cardiac event (CDI-PTSD). Supportive communication, realistic hope, and basic psychosomatic or psychocardiological interventions can reduce nocebo effects and anxiety spirals. In addition, this approach may help identify patients whose need for treatment should be discussed within a "Psycho-Cardio-Team" that still needs to be established.

title: Conduction System Pacing Versus Biventricular Pacing for Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is an emerging alternative to biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded divergent results, creating uncertainty about the comparative effectiveness.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CSP with BVP for CRT, searching PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through May 2026 (updating a prior review). The primary outcome was change in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF), analyzed with random-effects models and prediction intervals.

RESULTS: Eight parallel-group RCTs including 799 patients (396 CSP, 403 BVP) were included. Pooled ΔLVEF did not differ significantly (MD +2.40%, 95% CI -0.49 to 5.29, p = 0.091; I 2 = 75%). CSP showed a non-significant trend toward shorter paced QRS (MD -7.6 ms, p = 0.14) and improved NYHA class (SMD -0.33, p = 0.12). Heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.69), mortality (RR 1.17), complications (RR 0.84), and procedure time did not differ. The four trials enrolling exclusively LBBB patients favored CSP (MD +5.00%, 95% CI 3.01 to 6.98, p = 0.004; I 2 = 0%), consistent in the three using confirmed LBBAP/LBBP (MD +5.37%, 95% CI 3.23 to 7.52, p = 0.008; I 2 = 0%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of randomized trials of CRT, no statistically significant difference was observed between CSP and BVP for any outcome. Because no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and the clinical-event analyses were underpowered, these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence or comparable safety. Exploratory analyses suggest that patients with LBBB undergoing LBBAP/LBBP may derive incremental benefit, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.

METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).

RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.

CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

title: Safety and Outcomes of Transvenous Lead Extraction of Advisory ePTFE-Coated Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Leads: A Multicenter Experience With RELIANCE G.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE)-coated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are associated with progressive coil calcification and rising shock impedance, prompting a recent safety advisory. However, data regarding the safety and efficacy of transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for these chronic leads remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and procedural outcomes of TLE in patients with advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study at 13 centers of patients undergoing TLE of ePTFE-coated ICD leads. Primary endpoints included procedural success, complications, and short-term mortality. Multivariable analyses identified predictors of outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 423 patients undergoing extraction of advisory RELIANCE ICD leads (Boston Scientific), mean lead dwell time was 7.5 ± 5.3 years, and impedance-defined coil calcification was present in 15.1%. Laser sheaths were used in 63.8% of procedures and multiple extraction tools in 21.7%. Complete lead removal was achieved in 95.5%, clinical success in 98.8%, and extraction failed occurred in 1.2%. Major complications occurred in 0.9% of patients, with no procedural deaths. Calcified leads were associated with longer dwell times but not higher rates of major complications. Thirty-day mortality was 2.8%, primarily among patients undergoing extraction for infection.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, TLE of advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads was associated with high procedural success and low major complication rates despite long lead dwell times. Outcomes were consistent with contemporary TLE experience and do not suggest increased procedural risk attributable to this lead model. The presence of impedance-defined coil calcification did not adversely affect procedural outcomes, supporting TLE at experienced centers when clinically indicated.

title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease.
summary: Circadian rhythms, serving as a crucial temporal bridge linking neural activity and pathological biology, are regulated by central pacemaker neurons to maintain cellular homeostasis and coordinate diverse biological processes. Circadian rhythm disruption is closely associated with various diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Circadian rhythms are controlled by core clock genes, such as BMAL1 and CLOCK, modulating numerous physiological processes, encompassing metabolism, immune responses, neural activity, and hormone regulation. Circadian rhythms disruptions arising from shift work, jet lag, or inconsistent sleep schedules are implicated in both the onset and progression of numerous diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The article highlights how circadian dysregulation alters cellular processes to potentially accelerate disease progression. Circadian disruption results in impaired immune function, further promoting disease development and resistance to treatment. Potential therapeutic applications based on circadian biology, such as chronotherapy and personalized medicine, are also discussed. Recent technological advances, embodied in wearable devices and omics approaches, are increasingly providing deeper insights into circadian biology. Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.

title: Clinically Motivated Redesign of the Pennsylvania State University Child Ventricular Assist Device.
summary: Building on validated in vitro and chronic in vivo testing of the Penn State University (PSU) Child Ventricular Assist Device (CVAD), the four-bladed prototype rotor (Rev 0.0) was redesigned using established analytical and computational methods to improve hydraulic efficiency while preserving hemodynamic performance and biocompatibility. Applying turbomachinery principles at the nominal operating condition (3 liters/minute [LPM], 8,000 revolutions/minute [RPM]), a five-bladed design (Rev 1.0) was created with an ideal inflow angle (β1 = 41.0°) and outflow angle (β2 = 27.4°). In silico simulations of Rev 1.0 across the prototype's operating range (7,000-9,000 RPM, 1-5 LPM) demonstrated an approximately 40% improvement in hydraulic performance. The Rev 1.0 rotor was then evaluated on a benchtop mock circulatory loop using fresh ovine blood, confirming the in silico gains. The normalized index of hemolysis (NIH), measured at two clinically relevant conditions (1.5 LPM and 3.3 LPM, both at ~80 mm Hg), was 0.052 ± 0.054 and 0.047 ± 0.033 mg/dL, respectively, and high-molecular-weight multimers of von Willebrand factor were preserved within normal to borderline ranges. By achieving target flows and pressures at approximately 1,000 RPM lower speeds, the redesign reduces power requirements and enables longer untethered operation, advancing a fully implantable PSU CVAD toward a critical unmet need in pediatric advanced heart failure.

title: Comparison of virtual and true ECG-gated coronary CT angiography in patients with acute chest pain: a prospective cohort study.
summary:
PURPOSE: To compare the clinical value of true electrocardiogram-gated and virtual electrocardiogram-gated coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and to provide a reasonable and effective imaging strategy for patients with acute chest pain.

METHODS: A total of 254 patients with acute chest pain and suspected coronary artery disease who underwent CCTA were prospectively enrolled. Patients were alternately assigned according to examination date to the virtual ECG-gated group (n = 126), or the true ECG-gated group (n = 128). Examination time and radiation dose were recorded. Objectiveand subjective image quality parameters were evaluated. Objective parameters included image background noise, CT values of the aorta and coronary artery branches, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Subjective image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale. In patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography (ICA) within 30 days after CCTA, diagnostic agreement was evaluated using ICA as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed at the vessel level using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with the four major coronary arteries from each patient considered as the units of analysis.

RESULTS: (1) The virtual ECG-gated group demonstrated significantly improved examination efficiency compared with the true ECG-gated group, with a shorter total examination time (2.83 ± 0.37 min vs. 4.15 ± 0.49 min, P < 0.001) and positioning time (0.89 ± 0.26 min vs. 2.03 ± 0.35 min, P < 0.001). However, the radiation dose was higher in the virtual ECG-gated group than in the true ECG-gated group (3.58 ± 0.69 mSv vs. 3.18 ± 0.54 mSv, P < 0.001). (2) Image quality analysis showed that the virtual ECG-gated group had lower image noise than the true ECG-gated group, as well as higher SNR and CNR values for the aorta and coronary artery branches (all P < 0.001). However, CT values and subjective image quality scores were comparable between the two groups (all P > 0.05). (3) In the ICA-validated subgroup, the virtual ECG-gated group showed a higher diagnostic agreement rate than the true ECG-gated group (92.00% vs. 85.58%), with corresponding vessel-level AUC values of 0.89 and 0.82, respectively. However, the virtual ECG-gated group was associated with a higher radiation dose than the true ECG-gated group (3.58 ± 0.69 mSv vs. 3.18 ± 0.54 mSv), representing a trade-off for achieving an ECG-independent acquisition strategy and maintaining diagnostic image quality.

CONCLUSION: Virtual ECG-gated CCTA can significantly improve examination efficiency while maintaining comparable image quality and diagnostic performance to true ECG-gated CCTA. Although this approach was associated with a modest increase in radiation dose, this represents a trade-off for reducing dependence on real-time ECG acquisition and simplifying the CCTA workflow. Therefore, virtual ECG-gated CCTA may serve as a feasible and efficient imaging strategy for selected patients with acute chest pain, particularly in clinical scenarios requiring rapid evaluation or simplified workflow.

title: Polycystin dysfunction and cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD.
summary: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is one of the most common inherited kidney disorders characterized by the progressive formation of renal cysts. It is a systemic disease with significant extra-renal manifestations. Among these, cardiac electrical abnormalities are increasingly recognized as clinically important yet underappreciated contributors to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Beyond cyst formation, pathogenic variants in PKD1 or PKD2, which encode polycystin-1 (PC1) and polycystin-2 (PC2), respectively, interfere with calcium homeostasis, mechanotransduction, and mitochondrial function in both kidney and heart tissues. These molecular changes trigger a cascade of pathological events, including RAAS activation, TGF-driven fibrosis, and oxidative stress, leading to structural and electrical remodeling of the heart. These alterations contribute to cardiac electrical remodeling, manifesting clinically as QT interval and corrected QT (QT/QTc) prolongation, left ventricular hypertrophy, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and other electrocardiographic abnormalities. Despite growing evidence, cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD remain understudied in clinical practice. Early detection of subclinical cardiovascular abnormalities may be facilitated by electrocardiographic monitoring, cardiac imaging, and complementary biomarker assessment. Additionally, findings from iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte models support the translational potential of personalized drug-screening platforms. This review summarizes current evidence linking polycystin dysfunction to cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD by integrating molecular mechanisms with experimental and clinical findings. It also highlights the need for integrated cardio-renal approaches to improve cardiovascular surveillance, risk stratification, and future therapeutic development in ADPKD.

title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
summary:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.

RECENT FINDINGS: Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

title: Recurrent syncope with a type 1 Brugada electrocardiogram pattern in a patient on amitriptyline: Brugada syndrome vs. phenocopy-a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome is an inherited arrhythmogenic channelopathy associated with an increased risk of sudden cardiac death. Diagnosis relies on the presence of a spontaneous type 1 Brugada pattern on electrocardiogram (ECG). While multiple hypotheses have been proposed to explain its underlying mechanism, it is generally thought to be secondary to defective myocardial sodium channels. For this reason, sodium channel-blocking medications can induce a type 1 Brugada pattern, which may complicate risk stratification and raise the possibility of Brugada phenocopy.

CASE SUMMARY: A 44-year-old man on regular amitriptyline 75 mg for anxiety and panic disorder presented with two episodes of syncope. ECG showed classical features of a type 1 Brugada pattern. Routine blood investigations, including full blood count, renal function tests, a comprehensive electrolyte panel, and high-sensitivity troponin, were normal. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed normal cardiac structure and function. Following multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion, and guided by the 2022 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines, a shared decision was made to proceed with implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation. The patient was discharged with follow-up in the arrhythmia clinic and referred for genetic testing.

DISCUSSION: This case highlighted the diagnostic and management challenges of differentiating true Brugada syndrome from drug-induced Brugada phenocopy. Although our patient had type 1 Brugada ECG pattern in the context of amitriptyline use, his presentation with syncope complicates risk stratification. MDT discussion and reference to ESC guidelines played a key role in determining further management, which in this case was ICD implantation.

title: Homozygous LMNA (p.Arg216His) variant in an Ecuadorian patient with atrial flutter and high-grade atrioventricular block: a case report.
summary: Cardiac laminopathies caused by LMNA variants may present with conduction disease, atrial arrhythmias, and ventricular dysfunction, sometimes before overt ventricular dilation. We report a 42-year-old Ecuadorian man with recurrent syncope and progressive exertional dyspnea who developed atrial flutter with a markedly slow ventricular response, high-grade atrioventricular block, and severe bradycardia. Next-generation sequencing using the TruSight Cardio panel identified NM_170707.4(LMNA):c.647G > A (p.Arg216His) in a homozygous state. Franklin by QIAGEN classified the variant as pathogenic under the ACMG/AMP framework, although ClinVar contains conflicting interpretations and variant-specific functional and segregation studies were unavailable. Genetic ancestry analysis showed 89% Native American, 8.5% European, and 2.5% African ancestry. To our knowledge, p.Arg216His has not previously been reported in the homozygous state, whereas prior cardiac reports have involved heterozygous or compound heterozygous carriers, highlighting the novelty of this case report. This case expands the clinical and genotypic spectrum associated with LMNA-related cardiac disease and highlights the value of integrating electrophysiological, imaging, genomic, and ancestry data in underrepresented populations.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Biphenyl Derivatives with Therapeutic Potential for Atrial Fibrillation by Synergistically Inhibiting NaV1.5 Late Na+ Current and K+ Current.
summary: To overcome the side effects of conduction block and QT prolongation associated with antiatrial fibrillation (AF) drug dronedarone, a novel class of dual IKr and late sodium current (late INa) inhibitors was developed through computational modeling, chemical modification, and electrophysiological screening. Lead compound 8b retained potent IKr inhibition (IC50 = 1.5 μM) comparable to dronedarone. Crucially, 8b avoided dronedarone's peak INa inhibition while enhancing late INa suppression (IC50 = 2.5 μM) to counteract excessive QT prolongation and avoid conduction block. Compound 8b exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic properties (T1/2 = 5.02 h, F = 110% in mice, p.o.) and high ion channel selectivity. In an ex vivo rabbit heart model of AF, 8b demonstrated antiarrhythmic efficacy. Furthermore, 8b was effective in treating doxorubicin-induced heart failure in mice, a condition where dronedarone shows no therapeutic benefit. Collectively, 8b could serve as a potential new class III antiarrhythmic candidate.

title: Congenital Long QT Syndrome Type 2: Delayed Diagnosis After a Decade of Seizure-Like Episodes.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) is typically diagnosed in youth. Recognition in advanced age is rare and may be delayed when arrhythmic syncope mimics epilepsy.

CASE SUMMARY: A 93-year-old man with recurrent convulsive syncope presented with marked QT prolongation, notched T waves, and pause-dependent torsades de pointes/pulseless ventricular tachycardia initiated by premature ventricular contractions. Four years earlier, torsades de pointes had been attributed to mild hypokalemia and famotidine, although QTc interval remained prolonged after correction. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic KCNH2 frameshift variant, confirming congenital LQTS type 2. Advanced age, chronic kidney disease, and bradyarrhythmia likely reduced repolarization reserve. An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was discussed but not pursued after a goals-of-care discussion; leadless pacing was used to reduce pauses, and beta-blocker therapy continued.

DISCUSSION: Congenital LQTS may remain occult into advanced age when acquired factors reduce repolarization reserve.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Persistent QT prolongation after reversible factors are corrected should prompt consideration of congenital LQTS regardless of age.

title: It's about time: modeling circadian regulation of cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.
summary: Cardiac electrophysiology models resolve processes ranging from millisecond-scale ion-channel gating to hour-scale protein trafficking; yet, most do not explicitly represent circadian time. Consequently, ion-channel conductance, autonomic input, body temperature, and clock-regulated gene expression are often treated as fixed parameters or time-invariant inputs, causing simulated cardiac cells to correspond to an implicit and potentially arbitrary biological phase. In vivo, however, these factors vary across the ∼24-h cycle and jointly shape sinoatrial nodal pacemaking, ventricular repolarization, arrhythmia susceptibility, and drug response. In this mini-review, we examine recent efforts to incorporate circadian regulation into computational models of cardiac electrophysiology, including sinoatrial nodal and ventricular myocyte models of pacemaking, arrhythmogenesis, seizure-induced sinus arrhythmias, and drug-induced proarrhythmic risk. We synthesize these studies using a layered "source-transfer-target" organization in which intrinsic and systemic circadian sources act through source-specific transfer processes-including transcription, translation, channel trafficking, receptor-mediated signaling, and direct thermal modulation-to regulate shared electrophysiological targets. Building on this synthesis, we propose a general current-level formulation for incorporating circadian regulation of maximal conductance, channel gating, and ionic driving force into Hodgkin-Huxley-type models. Finally, we identify the experimental, computational, and clinical advances needed to translate these formulations into human-specific, personalized models of cardiac rhythm and arrhythmogenesis, with the long-term goal of enabling circadian-aware cardiac digital twins for time-resolved risk prediction and chronotherapeutic optimization.

title: Immunohistochemical markers for dating cardiac conduction system injury: current knowledge and forensic implications.
summary: The postmortem timing of myocardial injury remains a major challenge in forensic pathology, particularly when conventional histological methods are insufficient during the early hours after an ischemic insult. We conducted a critical narrative review of immunohistochemical markers for myocardial injury dating, focusing on their biological applicability to the cardiac conduction system (CCS). The search was performed using PubMed and Scopus; no date restriction was applied. Over the past three decades, markers including complement components (C5b-9), cardiac troponins, fibronectin, and connexin 43 have been investigated, with varying degrees of validation, for injury dating in working ventricular myocardium. However, the CCS - comprising the sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, bundle of His, and Purkinje fibers - is a histologically and molecularly distinct tissue that has received remarkably little attention in this context. We highlight fundamental differences in cellular composition, connexin expression profiles, extracellular matrix content, and baseline protein abundance between conduction and ventricular tissue that are likely to significantly alter marker behavior and temporal kinetics. The direct application of ventricular-based immunohistochemical timelines to the CCS lacks empirical support and may lead to forensic misinterpretation. The medico-legal implications are potentially significant, as accurate timing of conduction system injury is relevant to cases of sudden unexplained death, drug-induced arrhythmias, blunt cardiac trauma, and medical negligence litigation. Systematic, tissue-specific validation studies are urgently needed.

title: Embolic Myocardial Infarction From Delayed Left Bundle Lead Perforation.
A lightweight progressive residual convolutional network for interpretable arrhythmia classification.
summary: Arrhythmia poses a serious threat to human health, necessitating research into automated diagnostic methods. Although advances have been made in arrhythmia classification using deep learning, existing models often suffer from high computational cost and poor interpretability, limiting their clinical applicability. To this end, this paper proposes a lightweight progressive residual convolutional attention network (DResCA). Through the synergistic design of stage-adaptive downsampling and channel attention, this network reduces parameter redundancy while enhancing deep ECG feature extraction. To enhance clinical interpretability, template matching and attention visualization are employed to reveal the key ECG regions underlying the model's diagnoses. Five-class classification experiments on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database demonstrate that the model achieves 98.35% accuracy and 97.99% macro-F1 score while maintaining fewer parameters than mainstream deep learning models. These characteristics provide a practical technical pathway for real-time arrhythmia detection on wearable edge computing devices.
